messages.subject: Snapclust and HWE/PANMIXIA assumptions
messages.body_plain:
Hello Zhian and everyone,

Does somebody know if the clustering functions Snapclust or find.clusters(), can be applied to populations that are NOT UNDER HWE and are NOT PANMITIC? For example Pops with mixed reproduction systems (both clonal and sexual components present).

If not, which programs or commands can be used to find subgroups (k values) in pops with these characteristics?

Thanks a lot in advance

Vanina

messages.subject: ASSUMPTIONS FOR K-mean clustering?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Zhian and everyone,

I was wondering if someone can help me with the K-means clutering analysis. I am looking for information about the assumtions this method has or has not. According to the poppr examples and tutorial it can be applied in haploid, di- and ploly porid organisms and in clonal or recombinant population. But, I am wondering if someone has a reference or certain information about this assumtion for implementing this test?

IS HWE, LD, or something else assumed during this test? Are literature to cite regarding this info?

Thanks in advance,

Vanina Castroagudin

messages.subject: Re: conservative psex to account for possible HWE departures
messages.subject_clean: conservative psex to account for possible HWE departures
messages.body_plain:
Hello Hernán and Zhian,

I am interested in having the possibility to calculate Psex adjusted with Fis value for populations that depart from HWE. I was wondering if Hernán's suggestion has been incorporated into Poppr. If not, which would be the best way for me to calculate it, considering I do not have the programer abilities that Hernán has ( meaning -> I have no idea what to do with all that chunk of Code Hernan wrote, and how to use it myself inside R or Poppr)

Thanks,

Vanina

On Wednesday, March 11, 2020 at 11:54:01 AM UTC-4 herna...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello!
>
> During a review process realized it could be useful to calculate a conservative Psex when departures from HWE are expected (often the case with the organisms we work with) as suggested in
> https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-294X.2007.03535.x .
>  <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-294X.2007.03535.x>
>
> To do so I've replaced Pgen with the results from adegenet::inbreeding() (which are in essence Fis)  in the function Psex (see below). Maybe useful to include this function/option in a future version? :)
>
> psex_fis<-function (gid, pop = NULL, by_pop = TRUE, freq = NULL, G = NULL,
>           method = c("single", "multiple"), ...)
> {
>   stopifnot(is.genind(gid))
>   if (!is.null(pop)) {
>     gid <- set_pop_from_strata_or_vector(gid, pop)
>     by_pop <- TRUE
>   }
>   pop(gid) <- if (by_pop & !is.null(pop(gid)))
>     pop(gid)
>   else rep("A", nInd(gid))
>   if (!is.genclone(gid)) {
>     gid <- as.genclone(gid)
>   }
>   mll(gid) <- "original"
>   METHOD <- c("single", "multiple")
>   method <- match.arg(method, METHOD)
>   xpgen <- inbreeding(gid, res.type = "estimate", ...)
>   if (method == "single") {
>     nmlls <- rowSums(mlg.matrix(gid) > 0)
>     nmlls <- nmlls[pop(gid)]
>     G <- treat_G(G, nmlls, gid, NULL, "single")
>     pNotGen <- (1 - xpgen)^G
>     return(1 - pNotGen)
>   }
>   else {
>     pSex <- setNames(vector(mode = "numeric", length = nInd(gid)),
>                      indNames(gid))
>     for (p in popNames(gid)) {
>       pgid <- gid[pop = p]
>       pxpgen <- xpgen[pop(gid) == p]
>       mlls <- mll(pgid, "original")
>       mll_counts <- table(mlls)
>       ipgen <- which(!duplicated(mlls))
>       ipgen <- ipgen[order(unique(mlls))]
>       upgen <- pxpgen[ipgen]
>       sample_ids <- mlg.id <http://mlg.id>(pgid)
>       N <- treat_G(G, nInd(pgid), gid, p, "multiple")
>       pSexp <- mapply(make_psex, n_encounters = mll_counts,
>                       p_genotype = upgen, sample_ids = sample_ids,
>                       n_samples = N, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
>       names(pSexp) <- NULL
>       pSex[indNames(pgid)] <- unlist(pSexp)[indNames(pgid)]
>     }
>     return(pSex)
>   }
> }
>
>
>
> Best,
>
> Hernán Capador
>
> PhD student
>
>
> Sveriges lantbruksuniversitet
> Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences
>
> Department of Forest Mycology and Plant Pathology
>
> Box 7026, SE-75007 Uppsala
>

>
> Phone: +4618672706

> hernan....@slu.se, www.slu.se <https://www.slu.se/en/>
>
>
